overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data clearly highlights 'What If' hypothetical space scenarios and extreme planetary anomalies as the dominant growth drivers for FACTVERSE. Videos utilizing speculative planetary exploration ('What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?') combined with high-contrast comparative hooks achieve the highest views-per-day, strong like-per-view ratios, and active comment sections. Conversely, standard abstract brain facts and recycled psychological tricks with low engagement are losing traction.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views) significantly outperform standard encyclopedic facts published in the same period.
winning_patterns.action: Shift production focus heavily toward immersive, visually striking hypothetical planetary scenarios ('What if you stepped onto...').

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring bizarre physical realities like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views), 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views), and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,030 views) yield high click-through and sustained viewership.
winning_patterns.action: Continue sourcing bizarre, verifiable astrophysical extremes with strong visual metaphors for background rendering.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content like 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (71 views) and 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views) show stagnant growth and minimal viewer interaction.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological tricks and standard cognitive trivia unless paired with a high-stakes narrative or mystery.
